ic_name: ARM Serial Wire Debug (SWD) — ADIv5 (ARM IHI 0031C)
test_debug_features: SWD IS the debug architecture — the entire ADIv5 specification is a debug-access architecture. It exists specifically to enable in-system halt/resume, single-step, breakpoint, watchpoint, memory read/write, register read/write, and CoreSight trace access on Arm Cortex SoCs.
Halt / Resume: host writes the Debug Halting Control & Status Register (DHCSR) via MEM-AP to halt or resume the CPU core. DHCSR.C_DEBUGEN must be set first to enable debug mode.
Single-step: host writes DHCSR.C_STEP=1 + C_HALT=0 to step the CPU one instruction.
Software breakpoints: host writes BKPT instruction to instruction-memory via MEM-AP (BKPT raises a debug exception that is caught by DHCSR).
Hardware breakpoints (FPB - Flash Patch & Breakpoint unit): host configures the FPB comparators (reachable via MEM-AP) to match instruction-fetch addresses; on match the CPU halts.
Hardware watchpoints (DWT - Data Watchpoint & Trace unit): host configures DWT comparators for address / data / address-mask matching; on match the CPU halts and reports the matching comparator.

CPU register access: host accesses the Debug Core Register Selector (DCRSR) + Debug Core Register Data (DCRDR) registers to read/write any CPU register (R0-R12, SP, LR, PC, xPSR, MSP, PSP, PRIMASK, FAULTMASK, BASEPRI, CONTROL).
Memory read/write: host configures MEM-AP CSW + TAR + DRW to access any system-bus address; auto-increment via CSW.AddrInc enables bulk memory dumps.
Flash programming: host configures the SoC's flash controller (typically at a fixed AHB address) and writes flash pages via MEM-AP DRW transactions.

ITM trace (Instrumentation Trace Macrocell): printf-style trace packets emitted via the SWO trace pin (separate output pin, not part of the SWD protocol). The ITM is configured via MEM-AP-reachable registers.
DWT trace: data-watchpoint and PC-sampling trace packets via the SWO trace pin.
ETM trace (Embedded Trace Macrocell, optional): full instruction-and-data trace via the TPIU output pins.
CoreSight ROM Table at MEM-AP BASE address: host walks the ROM Table to enumerate every debug component on the SoC (CPUs, FPB, DWT, ITM, ETM, CTI, TPIU, ROM-of-ROMs).
CTI (Cross-Trigger Interface): allows synchronization of debug events between cores in a multi-core SoC.
Power-up / power-down debug: CSYSPWRUPREQ / CDBGPWRUPREQ in CTRL/STAT bring up debug power domains so the host can debug even when the SoC is in deep-sleep / standby.
applications_supported_by_swd_adiv5: Cortex-M MCU in-system debug (the dominant use case — covers virtually all M0/M0+/M3/M4/M7/M23/M33/M55 designs).
Cortex-M flash programming (debug probe drives the SoC's flash controller via MEM-AP).
Cortex-R real-time core debug (used in safety-critical automotive / industrial designs).
Cortex-A application core debug (typically alongside JTAG for boundary-scan + multi-core CTI).
Multi-core SoC debug coordination (each core has its own MEM-AP slot; CTI cross-triggers).
Production / factory test of Arm-based MCUs (SWD's 2-pin footprint allows smaller test points).
SWO trace capture for printf-style debugging without a serial UART (ITM port 0 acts as the printf channel).
Multi-drop SWD probing of dual-die packages or multi-core SoCs from a single 2-pin connector (ADIv5.2).

spec_provided_observability.name: DPIDR / IDCODE
spec_provided_observability.purpose: 32-bit DP fingerprint (designer + version + revision); always readable post-reset.

spec_provided_observability.name: CTRL/STAT sticky status bits
spec_provided_observability.purpose: STICKYORUN / STICKYCMP / STICKYERR / WDATAERR — host inspects to diagnose protocol-layer or AP-layer errors.

spec_provided_observability.name: TARGETID / DLPIDR
spec_provided_observability.purpose: ADIv5.1+ — identifies the target SoC + multi-drop target instance.

spec_provided_observability.name: AP IDR
spec_provided_observability.purpose: Identifies each AP's type (JTAG-AP, MEM-AP variants) + designer + revision.

spec_provided_observability.name: MEM-AP BASE → CoreSight ROM Table
spec_provided_observability.purpose: Enumerates every debug component on the SoC; host walks the table to discover what is debuggable.

spec_provided_observability.name: DRW posted reads
spec_provided_observability.purpose: Bulk system-bus memory readback via auto-incrementing TAR + RDBUFF flush.

spec_provided_observability.name: DHCSR (Debug Halting Control/Status)
spec_provided_observability.purpose: Reports CPU halted/stepped/locked status; reachable at a CoreSight-defined system-bus address via MEM-AP.

spec_provided_observability.name: ITM trace via SWO
spec_provided_observability.purpose: Printf-style trace packets emitted on the dedicated SWO trace pin.

spec_provided_controllability: MEM-AP DRW writes — write any system-bus address (including CPU control registers, flash controller, peripheral registers).
FPB comparator writes — configure hardware breakpoints.
DWT comparator writes — configure hardware watchpoints.
DCRSR + DCRDR — read/write any CPU register.
CTRL/STAT.CDBGRSTREQ / CSYSPWRUPREQ — request debug / system reset / power-up.
ABORT.DAPABORT — abort an in-flight AP transaction (used to recover from a hung MEM-AP).
fault_models_detected_by_swd: Parity error on Request packet — target drops the transaction; host sees subsequent FAULT (or all-zeros) until line reset.
Parity error on write Data — target sets WDATAERR; subsequent transaction returns FAULT; host must clear via ABORT.WDERRCLR.
AP transfer error (e.g. system-bus DECERR/SLVERR) — target sets STICKYERR; FAULT returned; host clears via ABORT.STKERRCLR.
Posted-read overrun (host issued too-many reads without flushing) — target sets STICKYORUN; FAULT returned; host clears via ABORT.ORUNERRCLR.
WAIT exhaustion (target persistently busy) — host-policy decides retry budget; typically backs off with longer SWCLK period.
Wrong APSEL / APBANKSEL (host targets non-existent AP) — AP IDR reads as 0; host detects missing AP and skips.
Line drop / connector unseat — host detects stuck-at-zero or stuck-at-one SWDIO and triggers reconnect logic (line reset + IDCODE).
notes: ADIv5 SWD is fundamentally different from JTAG boundary-scan: JTAG is a boundary-scan + test access architecture; SWD is exclusively a CPU + debug-bus access protocol. SWD does not implement boundary-scan cells, does not test board interconnect, and does not enable EXTEST/INTEST. The MEM-AP layer is what makes SWD universally useful — it lets the debug host pretend to be a bus master on the SoC's system bus, so it can read/write any memory or memory-mapped register including the CPU's own debug-control registers (DHCSR / DCRSR / DCRDR / DEMCR / FPB / DWT / ITM). The ITM trace via the separate SWO pin is the other half of the modern Arm debug experience (printf-style trace), but SWO is physically separate from the SWD protocol.
